## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$, a parameter $\xi\in F^\times$ of finite quantum
characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ with $\xi\ne1$, the level-one datum
$(\Lambda_0,0)$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ Cartan datum, the Hecke and KLR
towers with their blocks, and the symmetric level-one Fock model.

[F1] The quantum characteristic $e(F,\xi)$ and the requirement that a finite
quantum characteristic forces $\xi$ to be a primitive $e$-th root of unity in
the nondegenerate branch are as declared in
[[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]].

[F2] The level-one cyclic affine type-$A$ datum has all $d_i=1$, charge $0$,
and $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\langle\Lambda_0,h_i\rangle=\delta_{i,0}$
([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]).

[F3] The standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient is the quotient of the KLR
algebra by the first-strand cyclotomic ideal, with the diagrammatic grading
$\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2d_i$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]],
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]).

[F4] In the symmetric level-one model the node residues are $c-r$, the
standard vectors $M_\mu$ are indexed by all partitions, the restricted labels
are the $e$-restricted partitions of the given content and the empty component
is the basic crystal $B(\Lambda_0)$
([[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]).

[F5] The sign automorphism $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r$ is an involution of the
finite Hecke algebra and satisfies $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$ on the multiplicative
Jucys--Murphy elements ([[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]).

[F6] The Hecke side is $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$
(`prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras`),
whose residue-content blocks are the $e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$
(`def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks`); the blockwise
KLR isomorphism and the inherited transported grading are
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism` and
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading`, and the ordinary
Specht-form dictionary is
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell`.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The level-one cyclotomic relation.** By [F2], $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of the level-one Hecke presentation is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR first-strand cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i,0}}e(i)=0$ [F2, F3]. Consequently the level-one Hecke quotient is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra with $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ and its residue-content blocks are the $e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$, as stated by the level-one finite-Hecke supplier [F6]. [F2, F3, F6]

1.2 **The two sub-branches.** In characteristic zero a primitive $e$-th root of unity always exists, so (C0) is nonempty for every $e$; in characteristic $p>0$ the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ makes $X^e-1$ separable with $e$ distinct roots in the algebraic closure and the roots of unity form a cyclic group, so a primitive $e$-th root exists in $F$ exactly when the given $\xi$ is one, which the finite quantum characteristic guarantees [F1]. Thus in both branches $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity and $\xi\ne1$ as declared. [F1]

1.3 **Grading and transport conventions.** The KLR degrees are $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in the type-$A$ specialization with all $d_i=1$ [F3]. Transporting along the blockwise KLR isomorphism and an admissible local normalising series gives each Hecke block a $\mathbb Z$-grading, nontrivial on the corollary's level-one $e=2$ rank-two sector and trivial on a one-dimensional block, and two admissible series differ by the graded automorphism $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, so all graded multiplicities below are independent of the choice [F6]. [F3, F6]

1.4 **The Fock conventions.** The symmetric model has charge $0$, residues $c-r$, standard vectors indexed by all partitions, restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha$, and empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$; the conjugate of a restricted partition is $e$-regular [F4]. These are exactly the labels used by the global basis expansions of the page. [F4]

1.5 **The theta dictionary and content reflection.** The sign automorphism satisfies $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ and is an involution [F5]. On the finite level-one tower the Jucys--Murphy elements are the palindromic words $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1T_1\cdots T_{j-1}$; applying $\theta$ to this palindrome inverts the generators in reversed order, which reproduces the same palindrome inverted, and the $2j-2$ factors contribute $(-\xi)^{2j-2}=\xi^{2j-2}$, so $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$ exactly, the scalar $1$ being the product of the displayed factors [F5]. On a generalized eigenvector with $X_jv=\xi^iv$ one therefore has $X_j^{-1}v=\xi^{-i}v$, so pulling back along the involution $\theta$ reflects every residue $i$ to $-\xi$-power $i\mapsto-i$ and hence sends charge-zero content $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$; the ordinary module carries the conjugate content before pullback and is not identified untwisted in the same block [F5, F6]. [F5, F6]

2.1 **The ungraded convention dictionary and no choice.** After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is the $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, by the ordinary Specht-form comparison of [F6]; the Laurent-unit form factor of that comparison preserves radicals, so it includes the zero-quotient case and the dictionary is stable under applying the involution twice [F6]. The parameter $\xi$ of the Hecke algebra and the grading variable $q$ are kept independent, and no numerical relation between them is imposed. Every clause of the definition is a convention or a finite computation, so no choice principle is used. [F5, F6, given] ∎

items.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
items.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.

items.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
items.statement:
Work in the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition
$\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be
the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with
$S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a
two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is
defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module**
$$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$
a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$
([[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]]) fix a reduced decomposition
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put
$z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov--Lauda presentation
of `def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras`. For a
removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$
([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]) define
$$d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$$
(equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and
define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by
$\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$,
$\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing
$d$.

The definition asserts, and
`thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis` on this page proves,
that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of
$S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading
recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell
module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting
its grading, `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual`
identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape
independently defined ordinary Dipper--James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately,
`thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives
$S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are
two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate
module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to
$\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary
form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The
labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted
here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime with its partition parameters
$\mu$, $d=|\mu|$ and content $\alpha$, the Murphy cellular basis of the finite
type-$A$ Hecke algebra, and the KLR presentation of the block.

[F1] The regime supplies the field $F$, the parameter $\xi$, the level-one
weight, the Hecke and KLR towers, the blocks $H^\Lambda_\alpha$, the symmetric
residue convention and the independent grading variable $q$
([[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]).

[F2] The Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ and the cell/Specht modules of the
cyclotomic Hecke algebra are those of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]]; the
left module structure is obtained from the right cellular datum through the
star anti-involution.

[F3] Standard tableaux, their shapes, the row-reading initial tableau
$t^\mu$, removable and addable nodes, and the associated permutations $w_T$ are
as declared in [[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]],
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]] and
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]].

[F4] The sign automorphism $\theta$ is the involution of
[[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]], and $\theta$ commutes with
the star anti-involution.

[F6] The initial JM eigenidentity is the dominance-maximal case of
[[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] with the additive
JM elements of [[def-hecke-jucys-murphy-elements-and-q-contents]].

[F5] The KLR generators, their grading and the degrees $\deg e(i)=0$,
$\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The ideal and the cyclic generator.** The span $K(\mu)$ of the Murphy elements indexed by standard pairs of shape strictly dominating $\mu$ is a two-sided ideal by the cellularity theorem `thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular`, and the class $z_\mu=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is the canonical generator of the cell module [F2]. The left action is obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=mh^*$, so $S(\mu)=H^\Lambda_dz_\mu$ is a left module; no right module is identified with a left module without this conversion [F2]. [F2]

1.2 **The initial weight vector and block.** The row-filled tableau $t^\mu$ dominates every standard tableau of its shape at every prefix. Thus the triangular JM formula of [[thm-hecke-jucys-murphy-action-is-dominance-triangular]] has no off-diagonal terms at this vector. Star fixes $L_r$, so conversion to the left cell module gives $L_rz_\mu=[c-r]_\xi z_\mu$ for the node $(r,c)$ containing that entry. The multiplicative JM recurrence $X_{a+1}=\xi^{-1}T_aX_aT_a$ and the quadratic relation give $X_a=1+(\xi-1)L_a$: its inductive step is $L_{a+1}=\xi^{-1}T_aL_aT_a+\xi^{-1}T_a$. Hence $X_az_\mu=\xi^{i_a}z_\mu$ by $1+(\xi-1)[m]_\xi=\xi^m$, valid also for negative content. The weight idempotents and $y_a=(1-\xi^{-i_a}X_a)e(i)$ now give $e(i_{t^\mu})z_\mu=z_\mu$ and $y_az_\mu=0$. Since the vectors generated from $z_\mu$ have sequences obtained by permuting its residues, the whole cyclic module lies in content block $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$. [F1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

1.3 **The vectors.** For each standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$; the elements $z_T=T_{w_T}z_\mu$ and $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ are defined by left multiplication in the Hecke and KLR presentations, and $T_{w_T}$ is independent of its Hecke reduced expression, whereas $\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ can depend on the chosen reduced word: the KLR braid relation has correction terms [F5]. The resulting family is defined for the selected reduced words, and the discharge theorem proves that every selected family gives the same graded subspaces; it does not assert that the individual vectors are word-independent [F5]. [F4, F5]

1.4 **The degree recursion is well defined.** For a standard tableau $T$ of size $d>0$, $T_{\le d-1}$ is a standard tableau of the smaller shape and the node $A$ of $T$ containing $d$ is removable in that shape, so the recursion $\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ is a finite induction on $d$ with values in $\mathbb Z$ depending only on $T$ and $\mu$; the declared boundary count is evaluated in the same residue convention at every stage [F1, F3]. [F1, F3]

2.1 **The ungraded comparisons and Choice.** Forgetting the grading, the star-contragredient duality of `thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual` identifies the left cell module with the same-shape Specht dual, and the signed-conjugate comparison of `thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell` gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after conversion; since $\theta$ commutes with star by [F4], both comparisons keep their stated positions and neither asserts untwisted conjugate identification [F4]. Every construction selects finite sets of reduced decompositions and finite basis data, so no choice principle is used. [F2, F4, given] ∎

items.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
items.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.
items.strategy: Use the exact integer type-A KLR presentation with generator images in each characteristic-zero sector. Integer PBW straightening spans its image by ordered dot monomials times crossing words and word idempotents. Dot nilpotence in the finite characteristic-zero standard cyclotomic quotient bounds every position; finitely many words give finitely many nonzero spanning monomials. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. First descend to Q: the map from the Q KLR presentation to the generator image becomes the actual BK isomorphism after extending to K; faithful field extension makes it an isomorphism already over Q. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). For EVERY content alpha at fixed rank the reduced named generators satisfy the integer relations and generate F tensor the lattice, giving a SURJECTION H_alpha(F) -> F tensor H_alpha(Z) via the actual field BK presentation. Consequently dim_F H_alpha(F) >= dim_K H_alpha(K) for every alpha, including zero sectors. Sum over all finitely many rank-d contents: both total dimensions equal ell^d d! by the late field basis theorem. All individual nonnegative differences therefore vanish, proving every surjection is an isomorphism. Rankzero gives the singleton unit lattice; the levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero. Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. This is the complete applicable BK2008 Theorems6.1/6.4 proof route, without inferring an individual block dimension directly from total dimension alone. No choice.

items.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], define
$d^A(\lambda)$ for an ADDABLE $i$-node $A$ to be the number of addable
$i$-nodes strictly ABOVE $A$ minus the number of removable $i$-nodes strictly
ABOVE $A$. Define the codegree of a standard tableau $T$ by
$\operatorname{codeg}(\varnothing):=0$ and
$\operatorname{codeg}(T):=d^A(\mu^A)+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})$, where
$A$ is the node containing $d$ and $\mu^A=\mu\setminus A$. Define the defect of
a residue content $\alpha\in Q_+$ by
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha):=(\Lambda_0,\alpha)-(\alpha,\alpha)/2$ (the
symmetric form of [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). Then for every
partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$:

1. $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$ where $i$ is the residue of the removable
node $A$ and
$d_i(\mu)=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes of }\mu\}$;

2. $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$;

3. $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$;

4. $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$;

5. removing a brick does not change the codegree: if
$m\to_Tm+1\to_T\cdots\to_Td$ and $S=T_{\le m-1}$, then
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ whenever (i) $m,\dots,d$
occupy nodes in the first row of the first component of $T$, or (ii)
$d-m+1=e$ (the quantum characteristic).

No choice is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and a standard $\mu$-tableau
$T$, the addable and removable nodes of partitions, the symmetric form of the
cyclic affine type-$A$ Cartan datum, and the degree recursion of the graded
Specht definition.

[F1] Addable and removable nodes of a partition are as declared in
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]; node positions are
compared in the English diagram, with strictly above/below meaning in an
earlier/later row of the same component.

[F2] The degree $d_A(\mu)$ and the degree recursion
$\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

[F3] The root form has $(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)=a_{ij}$, and the level-one weight pairs by $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i0}$. These are the required symmetric-form conventions for [[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]; the root lattice and its positive cone are those of [[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]].

[F4] The weak Bruhat arrows $\to_T$ and the notion of a horizontal brick are
those of [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Counting addable and removable nodes (1).** Deleting the removable node $A$ of residue $i$ makes $A$ addable. Apart from this change, all corner changes occur immediately next to $A$ and have residues $i-1$ or $i+1$, which differ from $i$ since $e\ge2$ (for $e=2$ the two neighbor residues coincide with each other). Hence the signed count of $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ is unchanged, as is the signed count strictly below it. There is no other addable or removable $i$-node in the row of $A$. Splitting the signed corner count of $\mu$ into its above and below parts and the removable node $A$ therefore gives $d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$. [F1, F2]

1.2 **The Cartan formula (2).** Write $u_j$ for the basis vector indexed by $j\in\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$ in the free abelian group on residues, and choose $R$ greater than the number of nonzero rows of $\mu$. Put $b_r=\mu_r-r$. The signed corner vector is $\sum_i d_i(\mu)u_i=u_{-R}+\sum_{r=1}^R(u_{b_r+1}-u_{b_r})$: adjacent row-boundary terms cancel precisely when the corresponding node is not a corner, and the tail term cancels the artificial bottom boundary. For the empty partition this telescopes to $u_0$, so $d_i(\varnothing)=\delta_{i,0}=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)$. Adding a node of residue $j$ moves one $b_r=j-1$ to $j$ and changes this vector by $u_{j+1}-2u_j+u_{j-1}$. Thus each $d_i$ changes by $-a_{ij}$, including the double neighbor contribution when $e=2$. The vector with coordinates $(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$ has the same initial value and the same change when $\alpha$ increases by $\alpha_j$. Induction on the number of nodes proves (2). [F1, F3]

1.3 **Bricks in the first row (5)(i).** All nodes carrying $m,\ldots,d$ lie consecutively in one row, by [F4] and standardness; since they are the largest entries, they form the rightmost segment of that row. At every addition in the codegree recursion for a brick in row one, there are no rows strictly above, so the increment is zero. Summing these increments proves $\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le m-1})$. [F1, F4]

2.1 **The defect recursion (3).** Expanding, $\operatorname{def}(\alpha)-\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)-((\alpha,\alpha)-(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha-\alpha_i))/2=(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)-(\alpha,\alpha_i)+(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)/2=d_i(\mu)+1$ by (2) and $(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)=2$, which is the displayed recursion [F3]. [F3, step 1.2]

3.1 **Degree plus codegree (4).** For $d=0$ both definitions give $0=\operatorname{def}(0)$. For $d>0$ let $A$ be the node containing $d$ and $i=\operatorname{res}A$; by the induction hypothesis applied to $T_{\le d-1}$ and by step 2.1, $\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+\operatorname{codeg}(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$, where the middle equality uses (1) [F2, F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **Full residue bricks (5)(ii).** Suppose the terminal brick has $e$ nodes in row $r$ and occupies columns $c+1,\ldots,c+e$. Put $\lambda=T_{\le m-1}$. If $r=1$, step 1.3 applies. If $r>1$, standardness implies that all nodes in rows above $r$ already occur in $\lambda$ and that $\lambda_{r-1}\ge c+e$: each entry above a brick node is smaller, and all entries outside the terminal brick are at most $m-1$. Immediately before each of the $e$ additions, row $r$ therefore has length strictly smaller than $\lambda_{r-1}$. The signed corner counts strictly above row $r$ stay fixed throughout these pre-addition shapes. Indeed, in the top $r-1$ rows each maximal plateau of equal row lengths contributes one addable node at the start of its first row and one removable node at the end of its last row, and the last such row remains removable because its length is greater than that of row $r$ before the addition. Thus the number of addable corners above the brick equals the number of removable corners above it. The brick residues $(c+1-r),\ldots,(c+e-r)$ run through $I$ once. Summing the codegree increment for these residues counts each of the fixed above addable corners once positively and each above removable corner once negatively, giving zero. Hence the codegrees before and after the brick agree. The boundary count, defect recursion and tableau induction establish all five clauses by finite computations and use no choice. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.3] ∎

items.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
items.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an
equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends
finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift
$M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely
generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded
simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings
$\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. The inverse equivalence, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$, therefore
induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and
$G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and
the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$
(i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor
intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective
Hom-dualities $\#$ of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`,
and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual
indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha$. DEFINE the Hecke duality by
$\ast_H=\rho_\alpha\ast_R\rho_\alpha^{-1}$. This is a grading-preserving
anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of $e(i),y_r,\psi_r$, and $\rho_\alpha$
intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies
blockwise. This does not identify $\ast_H$ with the raw cellular
anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a
product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An isomorphism $\rho:R\to H$ of finite-dimensional unital
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras, possibly intertwining fixed grading-preserving anti-involutions
$\ast_R$, $\ast_H$.

[F1] The graded module categories, the internal shift $M\{r\}$, finite
generated graded projectives and the Grothendieck and Cartan data are those of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]],
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] and
[[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]].

[F2] The graded Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$,
its additivity, sesquilinearity and degree-zero part are those of
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]].

[F3] The Hecke-side grading and the block isomorphisms are supplied by
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` and
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`; the diagram dualities
are those of `def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals`, and
the left cell module used in the application is the one of
[[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Restriction of scalars is an equivalence.** Pulling back a graded left $H$-module $M$ along $\rho$ gives a graded left $R$-module with the same underlying graded vector space and action $r\cdot m=\rho(r)m$, and pulling back along $\rho^{-1}$ is a functor in the other direction; the two composites are the identity on underlying graded vector spaces and hence on objects and morphisms [F1]. Because $\rho$ is a bijection and preserves degree, the functor is exact, preserves finite-dimensionality, and satisfies $\rho^*M\{r\}=(\rho^*M)\{r\}$ [F1]. [F1]

1.2 **Projectives, Hom and composition multiplicities.** A finitely generated graded projective is a direct summand of a finite free graded module; pulling back preserves finite free modules and retracts, so it preserves finitely generated graded projectives [F1]. It is the identity on graded Hom spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{R,d}(P,\rho^*M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{H,d}(\rho_*P,M)$ and on shifts, so it preserves graded Hom dimensions and consequently composition multiplicities of graded simples together with their shifts; the graded Hom pairing of [F2] is therefore identified [F2]. [F1, F2]

2.1 **The Grothendieck identifications.** Since both inverse functors are exact and preserve split exact sequences, finite dimension and the shift, restriction along $\rho^{-1}$ induces $A$-linear isomorphisms $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R)\to K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R)\to G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H)$; the underlying module of a projective is carried to the underlying module, so the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$ are intertwined, and $q$ is preserved because shifts are [F1, F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.2]

2.2 **Dualities.** Suppose $\rho$ intertwines the stars. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$, the transported duality is $(a\cdot f)(m)=f(a^{\ast_H}m)$ on the dual space; substituting $a=\rho(x)$ and using $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$ shows that the duality computed with $\ast_R$ on $\rho^*M$ equals the duality computed with $\ast_H$ on $M$, so the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ are intertwined [F3]. The same substitution on $\operatorname{HOM}(P,R)\cong\operatorname{HOM}(\rho_*P,H)$ identifies the projective Hom-dualities $\#$; consequently normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives are preserved, since normalization is a shift-fixing condition [F3]. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The application.** For each nonzero content sector the block isomorphism $\rho_\alpha$ is a graded algebra isomorphism [F3]. Defining $\ast_H=\rho_\alpha\ast_R\rho_\alpha^{-1}$ gives an anti-automorphism because a conjugation of an anti-automorphism is again one, it is an involution because $\ast_R$ is, it preserves the grading because $\rho_\alpha$ does, and it fixes the named images $\rho_\alpha(e(i)),\rho_\alpha(y_r),\rho_\alpha(\psi_r)$ whenever $\ast_R$ fixes the corresponding KLR generators; the intertwining $\rho_\alpha\ast_R=\ast_H\rho_\alpha$ holds by construction, so the duality conclusion of step 2.2 applies blockwise [F3]. No identification of $\ast_H$ with the raw cellular anti-involution is made, and no product-fixedness is inferred from fixedness of factors. [F3, step 2.2]

4.1 **No choice.** The construction is the inverse-pair of functors induced by an explicit bijection, and every verification is a one-line substitution on generators or Hom spaces; no family of nonempty sets is selected. Hence no choice is used. [F1, F3, given] ∎

In the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] (both branches (C0)
and (CP)), fixing an admissible normalising series, the blockwise graded
isomorphism $\rho_\alpha:R^\Lambda_\alpha\to H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The nondegenerate level-one regime with its fixed admissible
normalising series, the blockwise graded isomorphisms $\rho_\alpha$, and the
standard homogeneous cyclotomic data on the KLR side.

[F1] The transport of the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups, its
Cartan maps, its forgetful maps, its graded Hom pairing and its diagram
dualities along a graded algebra isomorphism is the content of
[[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]].

[F2] The Hecke-side groups, Cartan map and pairing are the transported data of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] and
[[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]; the Hecke-side
induction and restriction functors are those of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]].

[F3] The type-$A$ specialization has $d_i=1$ and the finite loopless
cyclic quiver with arrows $i\to i+1$. For $e\ge3$, a forward adjacent pair
has $(h_{ij},h_{ji})=(1,0)$ and $Q^A_{ij}(u,v)=v-u$, while the reverse
pair has $(0,1)$ and $Q^A_{ji}(u,v)=u-v$; for $e=2$ both arrow
multiplicities are $1$ and $Q^A_{01}=Q^A_{10}=-(u-v)^2$. Nonadjacent
pairs have $Q^A_{ij}=1$. Thus in every case
$Q^A_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$
([[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]],
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]); the cyclotomic
quotient is the standard homogeneous one of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]].

[F4] The blockwise isomorphism, the grading, the finite-dimensionality and
symmetry of blocks are
`thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism`,
`cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading` and
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric`; the
KLR-side identifications, the functor action, the global bases and the crystal
correspondence are
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module`,
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module`,
`thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero`,
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`,
`thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis` and
`thm-simple-and-indecomposable-projective-crystals-agree-with-b-lambda`.

[C1] Choice is inherited through the highest-weight, crystal and global-basis suppliers of [F4];
the transport itself introduces none
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [F1]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport of the projective identification.** By [F1] the blockwise graded isomorphisms $\rho_\alpha$ induce an $A$-linear isomorphism $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)\to K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)$ which intertwines shifts, Cartan maps and forgetful maps, block by block and then on the restricted direct sums. Composing the inverse of this transport with the KLR-side isomorphism $\phi$ of [F4] gives $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$; the vacuum class is preserved because $\rho_\alpha$ is the identity on the underlying vector spaces and fixes the vacuum sector, and the divided powers are intertwined because the Hecke-side $E_i,F_i,K_i$ are defined to be the transported KLR functors [F1, F2, F4]. This proves (1). [F1, F2, F4]

1.2 **Transport of the module identification.** Applying the same transport to the exact functor on finite-dimensional graded modules gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)\to G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)$ preserving internal shifts, composition multiplicities and the diagram dualities, by [F1]. Composing the inverse of this transport with $\Psi_{\rm can}$ of [F4] gives $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ with the same restricted-weight-dual target, the same canonical module action transported through the functor, and normalized simple classes mapping to the form-dual projective basis; this proves (2). [F1, F2, F4]

1.3 **Functors and pairings.** The Hecke-side functors $E_i,F_i$ are by definition the images of the KLR functors under the blockwise equivalences, so the transported identifications intertwine them with the quantum action of [F4] [F1, F2]. The graded Hom pairing is identified by [F1], and the identity $h(P,M)=T(P^{\#},M)$ is the native comparison recorded in [F4] between the Hom pairing and the tensor pairing defining $\Psi_{\rm can}$; both are weightwise perfect on the normalized cover and simple bases because on those bases $P^{\#}=P$ and the actual unscaled cover/simple pairing clause of the module $G_0$ supplier makes the two pairings evaluate to the same delta, while the first-bar rule on shifts is retained on arbitrary shifted first arguments rather than identified with the bilinear form [F1, F2, F4]. This proves (3). [F1, F2, F4]

1.4 **Clause (4) and the type-A hypothesis check.** By [F3] the type-$A$ specialization has $d_i=1$, a symmetric Cartan matrix and the finite loopless cyclic quiver; for $e\ge3$ the ordered adjacent multiplicities are $(1,0)$ or $(0,1)$ and for $e=2$ they are $(1,1)$, giving exactly $Q^A_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ in both cases. Branch (C0) supplies characteristic zero, so all geometric-parameter hypotheses of the two global-basis theorems hold; transporting their conclusions along the blockwise equivalences identifies the normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives with the lower global basis and the normalized self-dual simples with the upper global basis [F1, F3, F4]. Since the transported functor preserves shifts and dualities, the crystals are the $B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals of [F4] and each class carries its label in the restricted set $RP$ [F3, F4]. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 **Both branches and Choice.** In an arbitrary branch of the regime the normalized finite-module duality representatives and their right crystal labels exist by the duality and crystal suppliers of [F4] alone, so clauses (1)-(3) hold in both branches and clause (4) only adds the characteristic-zero global-basis correspondence [F4]. No new choice is made: [C1] is inherited through the global-basis suppliers, and all transport verifications are finite substitutions. [C1, F1, F4, given] ∎

items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and
$r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the
Cartan matrix of the regime.

2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition,
then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$
in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and
$S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then
$\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$, standard tableaux $S,T$ of shape $\mu$, and the
degree function of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

[F1] The weak Bruhat arrows, the Garnir belt and tableau, the brick notion and
the terminal alternatives are those of
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]; in particular a
tableau below a Garnir tableau agrees with $t^\mu$ outside the belt.

[F2] The degree $d_A(\mu)$, the codegree recursion, the defect and the identities
$d_A(\mu)+d^A(\mu^A)=d_i(\mu)+1$, $d_i(\mu)=(\Lambda_0-\alpha,\alpha_i)$,
$\operatorname{def}(\alpha)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha-\alpha_i)+d_i(\mu)+1$ and
$\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$ are the content of
[[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]], including the brick lemma
$\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ for a removed brick.

[F3] The KLR generators, their degrees $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$ and
$\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, and the Cartan coefficients $a_{ij}$ of the
cyclic affine type-$A$ specialization are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]] and
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]].

[F4] Addable and removable nodes are as declared in
[[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **One edge (1).** Delete entries greater than $r+1$ from both tableaux. These occupy the same nodes and have equal degree-recursion contributions, so they cancel and we may assume $r=d-1$. Write $A$ for the node of $d$ in $T$ and $B$ for the node of $d-1$. In a weak edge $B$ is above $A$, and removing $B$ does not change the boundary counts strictly below $A$. Expanding the two recursions therefore gives $\deg S-\deg T=d_B(\mu)-d_B(\mu\setminus A)$. Removing the $i$-node $A$ changes the addable-minus-removable $j$-node count below $B$ by $a_{ji}$: when $i=j$ one loses a removable node and gains an addable one, giving $2$; at a single edge one loses one addable $j$-node or gains one removable $j$-node, giving $-1$; at $e=2$ the two adjacent colors coincide and the two contributions give $-2$; otherwise it gives zero. Thus $d_B(\mu\setminus A)-d_B(\mu)=a_{ji}$ and the desired difference is $-a_{ji}$. [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 **Reduced words (2).** The KLR element $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})$ is homogeneous of degree $\sum_l(-a_{j_l,k_l})$, where $(j_l,k_l)$ is the residue pair at the crossing after the generators to its right have acted, and the reduced word moves $t^\mu$ to $T$ by successive weak edges; by step 1.1 each edge changes the degree by the negative of the corresponding Cartan coefficient $a_{i_ri_{r+1}}=\deg\psi_re(i)$ [F3]. Summing over the $m$ edges gives $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu}))$, independent of the word because the degree is a function of $T$ [F2, F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The Garnir exchange (3).** By [F1], $S$ and $T$ agree outside the belt. The prefix shapes immediately before and after the belt coincide for $S,T$, so the outside-label contributions coincide. For belt labels, the rows strictly above its upper row are fixed. Their contribution to each upper-row addition depends only on that node's column, so the sum over the fixed upper-tail node set is identical. For a lower-row addition, subtract the local signed corners of the upper belt row from the actual above-node count. This leaves a fixed external signed-corner count: if the upper row reaches the length of the preceding row, the lost external removable corner and the suppressed local addable corner have exactly the same residue, so their changes cancel in this difference. The sum of that fixed correction over the lower-prefix node set is therefore identical as well. Thus outer contributions cancel in the codegree difference. Translate the belt row indices and residues to the two-row diagram $(m,b)$ with Garnir node $(1,b)$; the calculations below give these residual codegrees. The initial upper head has entries $1,\ldots,b-1$. The Garnir filling puts $b,\ldots,2b-2$ in the lower prefix, $r=2b-1$ at the upper node $(1,b)$, $r+1=2b$ at the lower node $(2,b)$, and the remaining entries along the upper tail. If $e=0$, the upper-belt contents $b-1,\ldots,m-1$ and lower-belt contents $-1,\ldots,b-2$ are disjoint, with each integer appearing once. Consequently the prescribed residue sequence $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ forces every belt label to occupy exactly its node in $s_rT$. That filling has $r+1$ above $r$ in column $b$, so is not standard. Thus no $S$ in the hypothesis exists for $e=0$; clause (3) is vacuous in that extension, without assigning a codegree to a nonexistent standard tableau. Now let $e\ge2$ be finite, and write $\delta_e(t)=1$ if $e\mid t$ and $0$ otherwise. In any standard two-row filling, a lower-row brick occupying columns $p,\ldots,q$ while the upper row has fixed length $x$ contributes $\sum_{c=p}^q(\delta_e(x-c+2)-\delta_e(x-c+1))=\delta_e(x-p+2)-\delta_e(x-q+1)$ to codegree: the addable upper corner has content $x$, the removable upper corner content $x-1$, and the added lower node content $c-2$. In particular a complete $e$-brick contributes zero, agreeing with [F2]. For $S$, the target belt residue word is the single consecutive run $-1,0,\ldots,m-1$ modulo $e$. Every lower brick starting after an upper brick has first endpoint indicator $1$, by comparing the preceding upper residue $x-1$ with the next lower residue $p-2$. Every lower brick has last endpoint indicator $1$: if followed by an upper brick this follows by comparing $q-2$ with $x$, while if it ends the whole belt then $x=m$, $q=b$, and the final prescribed residue gives $m-b+1\equiv0$. Hence every such brick contributes zero except possibly the initial lower brick, whose first indicator is $\delta_e(b)$ since $x=b-1$ and $p=1$. If $S$ starts instead in the upper row, its first residue forces $b\equiv0$, so the same total follows. Therefore $\operatorname{codeg}(S)=\delta_e(b)-1$. For $T$, the lower-prefix additions at columns $1,\ldots,b-1$ occur with upper length $b-1$ and contribute $\delta_e(b)-\delta_e(1)=\delta_e(b)$; the lower node in column $b$ is then added with upper length $b$, contributing $\delta_e(2)-\delta_e(1)=\delta_e(2)$; all upper additions contribute zero. Thus $\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\delta_e(b)+\delta_e(2)$. The matched residual count table is $$\begin{array}{c|c|r|r|r}e&b\bmod e&\operatorname{codeg}(S)&\operatorname{codeg}(T)&\operatorname{codeg}(T)-\operatorname{codeg}(S)\\\hline e>2&\ne0&-1&0&1\\e>2&0&0&1&1\\e=2&1&-1&1&2\\e=2&0&0&2&2\end{array}.$$ By [F2], degree difference is the reverse codegree difference at fixed shape and content. The vertically adjacent residues at $r,r+1$ are distinct and joined by one edge for $e>2$ and by a double edge for $e=2$; hence every row of the table gives $\deg S-\deg T=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$. All signs are accounted for by the explicit addable-minus-removable endpoint count. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **No choice.** The reductions use the finitely many nodes of the two tableaux, the finite belt and its finitely many bricks, and the finitely many residue comparisons; no family of nonempty sets is selected. Hence no choice is used. [F1, F4, given] ∎

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors
$v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions
$w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with
$a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of
$S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced
decompositions of the same $w_T$, then
$\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\lhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$;
in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is
independent of the choices.

3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ lie in
the prescribed homogeneous components; when nonzero their degrees satisfy
$$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$
Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis
$\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character
$\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$;
forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the
resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A partition $\mu$, its cell module $S(\mu)=H^\Lambda_dz_\mu$, the
standard vectors $z_T=T_{w_T}z_\mu$ and $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$, and the degree
function $\deg(T)$.

[F1] The module $S(\mu)$, the elements $z_T$, $v_T$ and the degree recursion
are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the Murphy
cellularity and ordinary dominance-raising Garnir straightening are
[[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] and
[[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]].

[F2] The weak Bruhat graph, the triangularity of the tableau order and the
Garnir/terminal alternatives are those of
[[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]; standard tableaux
and reduced words for $w_T$ are those of
[[def-young-tableau-standard-tableau-and-shape]].

[F3] The degree and codegree identities, including
$\deg(T)+\operatorname{codeg}(T)=\operatorname{def}(\alpha)$ and the brick
lemma, are those of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]]; the
shifted-degree formulas for weak edges, reduced words and Garnir exchanges are
those of
[[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]].

[F4] The KLR presentation, its grading and the degrees $\deg e(i)=0$,
$\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ are those of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]] and
[[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Ungraded straightening and triangularity.** The cellular Murphy straightening in [F1], in its left version, expresses $z_U$ for any tableau $U$ as a sum of standard $z_S$ with $w_S\le w_U$; row sorting is passage to the parabolic minimal representative, hence lowers Bruhat order; each Garnir replacement raises prefix dominance, hence strictly lowers Bruhat order by the row-boundary rank-count equivalence proved in [F2]. The standard $z_T=m_{T,t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ are independent because they are distinct surviving cellular basis elements, and they span the cyclic module by that straightening. The initial-vector calculation in the Definition gives $e(i_{t^\mu})z_\mu=z_\mu$ and $y_az_\mu=0$. In the fixed BK presentation, $\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_r(i))Q_r(i)^{-1}e(i)$, where $Q_r(i)$ has invertible constant term. Expand a reduced product and slide dots right using the mixed relations: the result is a sum $T_{r_{a_1}}\cdots T_{r_{a_b}}f(y)z_\mu$ over subwords, and the full-subword coefficient is a product of nonzero constants $Q_r(i)^{-1}(0)$. Rightmost dots evaluate at zero. The Hecke quadratic relation and the Bruhat subword criterion reduce each proper subword to $T_uz_\mu$ with $u<w_T$, so Murphy straightening gives $v_T=a_Tz_T+\sum_{S\lhd T}a_Sz_S$, with $a_T\ne0$ for standard $T$. This proves a basis for each selected reduced-word family and also straightens every nonstandard $v_U$ into standard $v_S$ with $S\unlhd U$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 **Filtered KLR word calculus before a grading on the module.** A dot moved through a crossing becomes the permuted dot plus a scalar term only for equal residues; moving all dots to the right thus deletes crossings in every scalar error. Two reduced words are connected by Coxeter moves. A distant move is exact; a length-three braid changes the product to a polynomial in dots times the remaining word, deleting the three crossings of that braid. A nonreduced word is shortened by bringing a repeated simple reflection together through these moves and replacing its square by its KLR quadratic polynomial. Induction on word length, using the deletion/subword criterion, therefore writes every error as $\psi_uf(y)e(i_{t^\mu})$ with $u<w_T$ and preserves its algebra degree. Acting on $z_\mu$ kills positive-degree rightmost dot monomials. Combined with step 1.1 this gives, without presupposing module homogeneity: reduced-word changes have only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$; $y_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$; and if $a,a+1$ share a row or column, $\psi_av_T$ has only $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ai_T$. For the last assertion first straighten below $s_aT$ and use the exceptional-prefix comparison of [F2] to get $S\unlhd T$; equality is excluded because adjacent same-row or same-column boxes have distinct residues for $e\ge2$. Weight support follows directly from $\psi_ae(i)=e(s_ai)\psi_a$ and commuting dots. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The simultaneous induction.** Assign degree $\deg T$ to the selected basis $v_T$. Prove together, for $m\ge0$, (a) word-change errors at standard tableaux of length at most $m$ have degree $\deg T$, and (b) all dot and crossing actions at standard tableaux of length at most $m-1$ have their prescribed degrees. The base $m=0$ has the unique length-zero tableau $t^\mu$ and no action assertion. For (a), a nontrivial braid error has at most $m-3$ crossings after step 2.1 and the same algebra degree as the original reduced word. Act on $z_\mu$ successively with the at most $m-3$ crossings of each shortened term, expanding after each action in the ungraded selected standard basis. Step 1.1 bounds every appearing standard-tableau length by the number of crossings so far, and step 2.1 gives the corresponding bound after straightening a nonreduced product. Thus before every action the standard-basis lengths are at most $m-4$, and the already proved action assertion (b) applies. No standardness of an arbitrary subword tableau is assumed. By [F3] the algebra degree plus $\deg(t^\mu)$ is $\deg T$. Strict-order straightening and weight support in step 2.1 therefore give exactly the difference formula (2). A sequence of braid moves gives it for any two words. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Dot actions in the induction.** At $\ell(T)=m-1$ write $v_T=\psi_av_U$ with $\ell(U)=m-2$; word changes only add shorter vectors of the same degree by step 3.1. Slide $y_r$ past $\psi_a$. The main term is $\psi_ay_{s_a(r)}v_U$, and the possible scalar error is $\pm v_U$ at equal crossing colors. The dot action at $U$ is homogeneous by induction and, by step 2.1, is supported on lengths strictly below $m-2$, so applying $\psi_a$ to all its basis terms is covered by induction. The mixed relation is homogeneous, so both the main term and the scalar error have degree $\deg T+2$. When $T=t^\mu$, the dot is zero. This proves every dot assertion at length $m-1$. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 **Crossing actions at standard swaps.** If $s_rT$ is standard and has length $m$, the word $s_rw_T$ is reduced, so the word-change assertion just proved at length $m$ and the weak-edge identity in [F3] give degree $\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$. If $s_rT$ instead has length $m-2$, write $v_T=\psi_rv_{s_rT}$ up to shorter same-weight same-degree errors. Apply $\psi_r$: the main term becomes $Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})v_{s_rT}$, and the other terms are crossing actions at strictly shorter tableaux. Those actions are covered by induction and the dot polynomial by step 4.1 and induction. Homogeneity of the quadratic relation gives the required degree also for this case. [F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **Crossing actions at a horizontal or vertical pair.** The four terminal alternatives of [F2] complete the crossing induction. For a distant terminal edge $t$, write $v_T=\psi_tv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, with $|t-r|>1$. Commute $\psi_r$ past $\psi_t$. The action $\psi_rv_U$ is supported strictly below $U$ by step 2.1 because the horizontal or vertical relation persists, so both successive actions are already covered by induction and their degree is the homogeneous product degree. For a two-edge terminal alternative write $v_T=\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ up to shorter homogeneous errors, where $\ell(U)=m-3$ and $r\pm1,r\pm1+1$ are horizontal or vertical in $U$. The braid relation rewrites $\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_rv_U$ as $\psi_{r\pm1}\psi_r\psi_{r\pm1}v_U$ plus the homogeneous dot correction. By step 2.1 the first action on the rewritten word is supported strictly below $U$, so all remaining actions use strictly shorter lengths and induction; step 4.1 handles the dot correction. The horizontal terminal base is $T=t^\mu$: step 2.1 makes $\psi_rv_T=0$. The vertical terminal base is the Garnir tableau. Here step 2.1 gives only $v_S$ with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=s_ri_T$, and the Garnir exchange formula in [F3] gives $\deg S=\deg T-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ for every such term. This proves (b), completing the simultaneous induction without assuming the homogeneity being proved. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Grading, character and independence.** The weight identity in step 2.1 and the action degrees established in steps 4.1–6.1 show that the vector-space grading is a module grading. Zero images belong to the stated homogeneous components; a degree is asserted only for a nonzero vector. Step 3.1 makes every change of selected reduced words a unitriangular basis change within each weight and degree, so it preserves the graded subspaces while individual $v_T$ may change. Finally the homogeneous basis yields $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_Tq^{\deg T}i_T$ and the construction used exactly the original ungraded left Murphy cell. Every selection is finite and requires no choice principle. [F1, F4, step 3.1, step 6.1, algebra] ∎
